annotations.description: MiMo Worrier skipped their land drop on turn 2 with three lands in hand. Missing a land drop this early is a significant tempo loss, especially when they have a 3-drop (Formidable Speaker) they'd want to cast on turn 3. Playing a land costs nothing and is pure upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to play any land on turn 2, despite having Breeding Pool, Gloomlake Verge, and Willowrush Verge in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Breeding Pool (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped, or tapped if preserving life) to enable casting Formidable Speaker on turn 3 with access to green mana. Gloomlake Verge would also be a reasonable choice since it provides black mana with the Watery Grave already in play.

annotations.description: Paid 2 life for Breeding Pool when Willowrush Verge would have provided the same colors (U and G, since Watery Grave is an Island) for free. There was no 2-mana spell to cast this turn that required the untapped land, making the life payment completely unnecessary even if Breeding Pool were the right land to play.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Breeding Pool paying 2 life to enter untapped
annotations.betterLine: Play Willowrush Verge, which enters untapped for free and provides both U and G (since Watery Grave is an Island), saving 2 life and preserving Breeding Pool for a turn where its dual land type or specific timing matters more.

annotations.description: On turn 2 with only 2 lands (Watery Grave and Demolition Field), the player activated Demolition Field's sacrifice ability for 2 mana. This costs {2}, {T}, and sacrifices the land, meaning they spend both their lands to use this ability and are left with 0 lands on board. They have Gloomlake Verge, Island, Island, Swamp in hand but haven't played their land for the turn yet. Even if they play a land after this resolves, they'll be down to 1 land on board. This is a catastrophic tempo loss on turn 2 - they're destroying one of the opponent's dual lands (which the opponent can replace with a basic) while setting themselves back enormously on mana development. They have Deadly Cover-Up (5 mana) and Stock Up (3 mana) in hand that they need to cast, and this play delays them by multiple turns. The opponent also gets to search for a basic land, so it's not even denying them a color permanently.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Demolition Field's sacrifice ability on turn 2, spending all available mana and sacrificing one of only two lands to destroy an opponent's nonbasic land.
annotations.betterLine: Play Gloomlake Verge as land for turn, tap Watery Grave and Demolition Field for mana if needed, and develop mana base normally. Save Demolition Field for later when its tempo cost is less significant, or simply use it as a colorless mana source. The priority should be hitting land drops and reaching 3 mana for Stock Up or 5 mana for Deadly Cover-Up.

annotations.description: Activating Demolition Field's destroy ability on turn 3 costs 2 mana + tap + sacrifice, leaving GPT4om Gramps with only Watery Grave (1 land) after this resolves. The opponent gets to search for a basic land, so they net a land while GPT4om Gramps searches for one basic but sacrificed one, effectively trading down. More critically, GPT4om Gramps has only 2 lands in play and needs to develop mana to cast Deadly Cover-Up (5 mana) and Stock Up (3 mana). Sacrificing Demolition Field on turn 3 when the opponent has no threatening board presence (just lands, no creatures) sets back mana development significantly. The opponent's lands (Watery Grave, Breeding Pool, Willowrush Verge) aren't providing any unique strategic advantage worth destroying at the cost of falling behind on mana. Additionally, both players search for basics, so the opponent replaces their destroyed land.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Demolition Field's sacrifice ability to destroy an opponent's nonbasic land on turn 3 with only 2 lands in play and no board pressure from the opponent.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Demolition Field for {C} mana or simply play a land from hand (Gloomlake Verge, Island, or Swamp) and pass, developing mana toward casting Stock Up on turn 4 or Deadly Cover-Up on turn 5. Demolition Field should be saved for later when mana is less constrained or when destroying a specific land is strategically important.

annotations.description: GPT4om Gramps cast Stock Up before playing a land. They have Gloomlake Verge, Island, Undercity Sewers, and Swamp in hand. They should play a land first (likely Undercity Sewers for the surveil trigger before drawing, or Gloomlake Verge to have 4 mana available). By casting Stock Up first with only 3 lands, they use all their mana and miss the opportunity to surveil before the draw spell (if playing Undercity Sewers) or to have mana available after resolving Stock Up. Playing land before spells is fundamental sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Stock Up before playing a land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Undercity Sewers first (to surveil 1 before drawing, improving Stock Up selection quality), then cast Stock Up using the three untapped lands (Watery Grave + 2x Demolition Field).

annotations.description: Activating Demolition Field before playing a land for the turn. With Gloomlake Verge, Island, Swamp, and Undercity Sewers in hand, playing a land first would leave mana available after the activation to hold up Essence Scatter (1U) or Requiting Hex (B). Additionally, using Demolition Field on Turn 4 to destroy an opponent's land when the opponent only has a 2/4 creature and the priority should be developing mana for Deadly Cover-Up or holding up countermagic is questionable.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Demolition Field's destroy-land ability before playing a land, using all available mana on Turn 4.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (e.g., Gloomlake Verge or Island), then either hold up Essence Scatter/Requiting Hex for interaction, or if still wanting to use Demolition Field, do so while retaining mana for a response.

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Gloomlake Verge is slightly suboptimal. Gloomlake Verge produces both U and B (since they already control an Island via Watery Grave and a Swamp), so it's strictly better than a basic Swamp here - it provides the same black mana plus blue mana flexibility. Additionally, keeping basic lands in hand is better for future Demolition Field activations or in case the opponent has land destruction that cares about nonbasics. However, Gloomlake Verge entering untapped and producing both colors is more valuable than a basic Swamp right now, especially with Essence Scatter in hand wanting UU availability. With Swamp played, they have access to 1U + 2B, but with Gloomlake Verge they'd have access to 2U + 1B (or 1U + 2B), giving more flexibility for Essence Scatter.
annotations.actionTaken: Played basic Swamp as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Gloomlake Verge to maximize mana flexibility, keeping basic Swamp in hand for future turns. This gives better access to blue mana for Essence Scatter while still enabling black mana.

annotations.description: Activating Demolition Field to destroy an opponent's nonbasic land when the opponent already has 5 lands and an Overlord of the Balemurk with impending on board provides minimal disruption. The opponent gets to search for a basic, largely negating the mana denial. The Demolition Field could have been kept for later when color-screwing the opponent matters more, or the mana could have been used differently.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Demolition Field's sacrifice ability to destroy an opponent's nonbasic land on turn 5.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land from hand, hold Demolition Field for a more impactful moment, and keep mana up for Essence Scatter or Requiting Hex. Focus on reaching 5 mana for Deadly Cover-Up as the primary game plan.

annotations.description: Destroying Watery Grave is suboptimal because it produces U/B which the opponent has redundant sources for (Undercity Sewers, Gloomlake Verge). The opponent replaces it with a basic that still enables their UB mana. Willowrush Verge is the only green mana source on board, and destroying it would likely cut the opponent off green entirely since the replacement basic land wouldn't produce green.

annotations.betterLine: Target Willowrush Verge to cut off the opponent's green mana, which is their splash color and harder to replace with a basic land search

annotations.betterLine: Play Gloomlake Verge, which enters untapped and can tap for either U or B, providing strictly better mana flexibility for casting both Deadly Cover-Up and Requiting Hex
